title: Sorting & Categorising Words
keyIdea: Words can be put into groups. Things of the same kind go together, like animals or food. To sort, pick a rule and check every card against it. Change the rule and the groups change. Some words come in pairs of opposites, like big and small: an opposite is at the other end, not nearly the same.

kid: A dog, a cat and a cow are all animals. So they go in one group. An apple and a banana are food. They go in a new group.
To find the odd one out, look for what the others share. Apple, banana and grapes are fruit. A car is not. So the car is the odd one out.
You can sort the same things in a new way. By colour, a red strawberry goes with a red fire truck. By kind, the strawberry goes with food. The rule picks the groups.
Some words are opposites. Big and small. Hot and cold. Up and down. An opposite is at the other end. Warm is not the opposite of hot. Cold is.
adult: This topic is for ages 5 to 8. Sorting words into groups such as animals, food, clothes and vehicles builds the links between words that make vocabulary stick. A child who can say why a lion and a tiger go together, and why a chair does not, is learning the idea of a category, which later supports definitions, science classification and writing.

Two habits matter. First, name the rule before sorting and test every item against it. Second, notice that the same objects can be sorted more than one way: by colour, by size, or by what kind of thing they are. Asking "Why do these go together?" makes your child say the rule out loud, which is the real skill.

Common mistakes: grouping by how things look (all red, all round) when the task is about what kind of thing they are; switching rules halfway through a sort; choosing a near-synonym as an opposite (warm for hot, huge for big); and choosing a word that simply goes with the first one (sun for hot, door for open). Be careful with a group reason that fits only some of the items: a good reason fits every one.

In the lab your child drags picture cards into Animals and Food, finds the odd one out in three groups, sorts the same four cards first by colour and then by kind, picks the reason a group belongs together, and matches four pairs of opposites. Every drag can also be done with a big button.

familyTip: At tidy-up time, ask your child to sort toys into two groups and tell you the rule. Then ask for a new rule for the same toys. On walks, play "What is the opposite?" with words like up, wet, loud and fast.

practice.prompt: Which one does not belong: 🐶 dog, 🐱 cat, 🚗 car, 🐰 rabbit?
practice.hint: Three of them are animals. Which one is not?
practice.explain: Dog, cat and rabbit are animals. A car is not an animal, so it is the odd one out.

practice.prompt: Mia has {n} apples and {n} bananas. Which group do they all go in?
practice.hint: Can you eat an apple? Can you eat a banana?
practice.explain: Apples and bananas are both food, so all {=2*n} go in the Food group.

practice.prompt: What is the opposite of cold?
practice.hint: An opposite is at the other end. Cool is only a little bit cold.
practice.explain: Hot is the opposite of cold. Cool means a bit cold, and ice just goes with cold.

practice.prompt: We sort {n} toys by colour. Where does a red ball go?
practice.hint: The rule is colour. What colour is the ball?
practice.explain: When the rule is colour, a red ball goes with the red things, whatever kind of toy it is.

practice.prompt: 🧢 hat, 🧤 gloves, 🧣 scarf. Why do they go together?
practice.hint: What do you do with a hat, gloves and a scarf?
practice.explain: You wear all three, so they are clothes. They are not all red, and they are not toys.

pool.prompt: Which one does not belong: 🍎 apple, 🍌 banana, 🪑 chair, 🍇 grapes?
pool.hint: Look for what three of them share.
pool.explain: Apple, banana and grapes are fruit. A chair is not fruit, so it does not belong.

pool.prompt: What is the opposite of big?
pool.hint: Huge means very big. Find the word at the other end.
pool.explain: Small is the opposite of big. Huge means nearly the same as big.

pool.prompt: What is the opposite of stop?
pool.hint: What does a green light tell you to do?
pool.explain: Go is the opposite of stop. Wait is nearly the same as stop, and red just goes with stop.

pool.prompt: Sam sorts {n} cards into Animals and Food. Where does a 🐸 frog go?
pool.hint: Is a frog something that is alive and moves, or something you eat?
pool.explain: A frog is an animal. It hops and eats flies, so it goes in Animals.

pool.prompt: A strawberry and a fire truck are both red. Can they go in the same group?
choices: Yes, if the rule is colour
pool.explain: If you sort by colour, they go together. If you sort by kind, they do not. The rule decides.

pool.prompt: 🐟 fish, 🐙 octopus, 🐳 whale. Why do they go together?
choices: They all live in the sea
pool.hint: Where would you find all three?
pool.explain: All three live in the sea. They cannot fly, and a whale is not small.

pool.prompt: Zoe has {n} 🚗 cars, a 🚌 bus and a 🍞 loaf of bread. Which is the odd one out?
pool.hint: Which ones can take you places?
pool.explain: Cars and a bus take you places. Bread does not, so the bread is the odd one out.

pool.prompt: What is the opposite of up?
pool.hint: Point up. Now point the other way.
pool.explain: Down is the opposite of up. High is nearly the same as up, and the sky just goes with up.

pool.prompt: Leo sorts by kind: food or things that go. Where does a 🚕 taxi go?
pool.hint: The rule is kind, not colour.
pool.explain: A taxi is a thing that goes. Yellow is a colour, but the rule here is kind.

visual.caption: Is it an animal or food? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: drag cards into groups, find the odd one out, sort the same cards by a new rule, say why a group goes together, match opposites.
